answer: A survey cooperative tracking falcon nests and violet patches in karst country could charge a nonrefundable POA burn for each governance vote, with no free vote per account. The contract accepts each burn receipt once, bound to the proposal and ballot, so replaying it or spreading burns across aliases adds no voting power per coin spent. Buying 100 votes requires 100 burns regardless of identity count. Set the burn against the value at risk and cap aggregate treasury outflows. This prices vote flooding; it does not prove unique humans or stop a wealthy cartel.
